contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #145: Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem.

Fix k>=3 and a probability law on a k by k array of standard-Borel cell spaces, at a typical fixed parameter E. Assume exactly the numbered and grouped conditional kernels of Proposition square-locality in staged sections/03-arrays.tex; no interchange of axes, no bounded inverse, and no algebra structure on active intersections is assumed.

definitions.active: Closed linear span in the chosen cell L2 of conditional expectations of bounded tests of the other entries of its full row or column.
definitions.exact_line: A line generated by a modulus-one cell function participating in a constant-product modulus-one tuple for the full row or column law.
definitions.grouped: Every ordered partition of the row index set and column index set into three nonempty groups, with the original axis order retained.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 145 (Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem.; papers: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/145.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Under the full inherited square-locality hypotheses, every row-active projection commutes with the column-active projection at its cell, and their intersection is the closed span of the lines exact simultaneously for the full k-coordinate row and column laws. The intersection is L2 of a compact metrizable abelian Haar factor, and every incident conditional Markov operator restricts almost surely to a unitary between the corresponding intersections.
The grouped rectangle identities imply active-projection commutation, opposite-axis intertwining, and essential totality of every edge and reverse edge on the common active spaces.

The restricted grouped rectangle has parameter-independent injective source and target squares. Its polar unitaries normalize into a common closed abelian group with invariant probability and a measurable corner ratio.

The projection identities for row and column tensor contractions hold on all L2 inputs; restricted contractions span each common active space. Consequently the corner common active space equals L2 of its normalized polar ratio, with a basis of simultaneously exact unimodular lines.

Coincidence of the orthogonal exact-line families over all three-block splits implies full-coordinate simultaneous exactness for every k>=3; edge partner transport then makes the common-active edge restrictions unitary.

For bounded maps between four arbitrary Hilbert spaces, the two typed rectangle identities imply all four square-intertwining identities. A fixed source square of a family whose adjoint ranges are total is injective, and continuous operators can be cancelled on dense ranges without a bounded inverse. This is only the functional-analytic algebraic core, not the full probability theorem.

The independent product of a binary row-and-column parity square, two row-only parity squares, one column-only parity square and one fully independent square satisfies every three-cell square-locality hypothesis exactly. At a cell the row-active, column-active and common dimensions are respectively 8, 4 and 2, and all contraction-projection and unitary-transport identities hold. This finite experiment does not prove the standard-Borel theorem.

For bounded maps between four arbitrary Hilbert spaces, the two typed rectangle identities imply all four square-intertwining identities. A fixed source square of a family whose adjoint ranges are total is injective, and continuous operators can be cancelled on dense ranges without a bounded inverse. This is only the functional-analytic algebraic core, not the full probability theorem.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
import Mathlib.Topology.DenseEmbedding

noncomputable section

open scoped InnerProduct

namespace OperatorSquare

variable {H1 H2 H3 H4 : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup H1] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H1] [CompleteSpace H1]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H2] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H2] [CompleteSpace H2]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H3] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H3] [CompleteSpace H3]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H4] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H4] [CompleteSpace H4]

theorem rectangle_squares
    (F : H2 →L[ℂ] H1) (G : H4 →L[ℂ] H3)
    (K : H3 →L[ℂ] H1) (N : H4 →L[ℂ] H2)
    (h1 : F ∘L N = K ∘L G)
    (h2 : F† ∘L K = N ∘L G†) :
    ((K ∘L K†) ∘L F = F ∘L (N ∘L N†)) ∧
    ((K† ∘L K) ∘L G = G ∘L (N† ∘L N)) ∧
    ((F† ∘L F) ∘L N = N ∘L (G† ∘L G)) ∧
    ((F ∘L F†) ∘L K = K ∘L (G ∘L G†)) := by
  have h2star : K† ∘L F = G ∘L N† := by
    simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_adjoint]
      using congrArg (fun T => T†) h2
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · calc
      (K ∘L K†) ∘L F = K ∘L (K† ∘L F) := by
        simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = K ∘L (G ∘L N†) := by rw [h2star]
      _ = (K ∘L G) ∘L N† := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = (F ∘L N) ∘L N† := by rw [h1]
      _ = F ∘L (N ∘L N†) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
  · calc
      (K† ∘L K) ∘L G = K† ∘L (K ∘L G) := by
        simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = K† ∘L (F ∘L N) := by rw [h1]
      _ = (K† ∘L F) ∘L N := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = (G ∘L N†) ∘L N := by rw [h2star]
      _ = G ∘L (N† ∘L N) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
  · calc
      (F† ∘L F) ∘L N = F† ∘L (F ∘L N) := by
        simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = F† ∘L (K ∘L G) := by rw [h1]
      _ = (F† ∘L K) ∘L G := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = (N ∘L G†) ∘L G := by rw [h2]
      _ = N ∘L (G† ∘L G) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
  · calc
      (F ∘L F†) ∘L K = F ∘L (F† ∘L K) := by
        simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = F ∘L (N ∘L G†) := by rw [h2]
      _ = (F ∘L N) ∘L G† := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = (K ∘L G) ∘L G† := by rw [h1]
      _ = K ∘L (G ∘L G†) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]

theorem fixed_target_squares {X C D : Type*} [Nonempty D]
    (F : X → H2 →L[ℂ] H1) (K : C → H3 →L[ℂ] H1)
    (N : D → H4 →L[ℂ] H2)
    (htotal : Dense (Submodule.span ℂ {v : H1 | ∃ x w, F x w = v} : Set H1))
    (heq : ∀ c x d,
      (K c ∘L (K c)†) ∘L F x = F x ∘L (N d ∘L (N d)†)) :
    ∀ c c', K c ∘L (K c)† = K c' ∘L (K c')† := by
  classical
  let d : D := Classical.choice inferInstance
  intro c c'
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext_on htotal
  rintro v ⟨x, w, rfl⟩
  calc
    (K c ∘L (K c)†) (F x w)
        = (F x ∘L (N d ∘L (N d)†)) w :=
      congrArg (fun T : H2 →L[ℂ] H1 => T w) (heq c x d)
    _ = (K c' ∘L (K c')†) (F x w) :=
      (congrArg (fun T : H2 →L[ℂ] H1 => T w) (heq c' x d)).symm

theorem total_adjoint_fixed_square_injective {I : Type*}
    (F : I → H1 →L[ℂ] H2) (S : H1 →L[ℂ] H1)
    (hsquare : ∀ i, (F i)† ∘L F i = S)
    (htotal : ∀ v : H1,
      (∀ i w, inner ℂ ((F i)† w) v = 0) → v = 0) :
    Function.Injective S := by
  intro u v huv
  have hS : S (u - v) = 0 := by simp [map_sub, huv]
  have hzero : u - v = 0 := by
    apply htotal (u - v)
    intro i w
    have hmem : u - v ∈ ((F i)† ∘L F i).ker := by
      change ((F i)† ∘L F i) (u - v) = 0
      rw [hsquare i]
      exact hS
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.ker_adjoint_comp_self] at hmem
    change F i (u - v) = 0 at hmem
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, hmem, inner_zero_right]
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp hzero

theorem cancel_dense_range
    (A : H1 →L[ℂ] H2) (S T : H2 →L[ℂ] H3)
    (hA : DenseRange A) (heq : S ∘L A = T ∘L A) : S = T := by
  have hfun : (fun x => S x) = (fun x => T x) :=
    hA.equalizer S.continuous T.continuous (by
      funext x
      exact congrArg (fun Q : H1 →L[ℂ] H3 => Q x) heq)
  ext x
  exact congrFun hfun x

theorem contraction_projection
    (C : H2 →L[ℂ] H3 →L[ℂ] H1)
    (P0 : H1 →L[ℂ] H1) (P1 : H2 →L[ℂ] H2) (P2 : H3 →L[ℂ] H3)
    (hP2 : ∀ h, P2 (P2 h) = P2 h)
    (hleft : ∀ g h, P0 (C g h) = C g (P2 h))
    (hright : ∀ g h, P0 (C g h) = C (P1 g) h) :
    ∀ g h, P0 (C g h) = C (P1 g) (P2 h) := by
  intro g h
  calc
    P0 (C g h) = C g (P2 h) := hleft g h
    _ = P0 (C g (P2 h)) := by
      have heq := hleft g (P2 h)
      rw [hP2] at heq
      exact heq.symm
    _ = C (P1 g) (P2 h) := hright g (P2 h)

end OperatorSquare

      _ = (F ∘L N) ∘L N† := by rw [h1]
      _ = F ∘L (N ∘L N†) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]

      _ = (N ∘L G†) ∘L G := by rw [h2]
      _ = N ∘L (G† ∘L G) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
  · calc
      (F ∘L F†) ∘L K = F ∘L (F† ∘L K) := by
        simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = F ∘L (N ∘L G†) := by rw [h2]
      _ = (F ∘L N) ∘L G† := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = (K ∘L G) ∘L G† := by rw [h1]
      _ = K ∘L (G ∘L G†) := by simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]

    (N : D → H4 →L[ℂ] H2)
    (htotal : Dense (Submodule.span ℂ {v : H1 | ∃ x w, F x w = v} : Set H1))

theorem total_adjoint_fixed_square_injective {I : Type*}
    (F : I → H1 →L[ℂ] H2) (S : H1 →L[ℂ] H1)
    (hsquare : ∀ i, (F i)† ∘L F i = S)
    (htotal : ∀ v : H1,
      (∀ i w, inner ℂ (((F i)†) w) v = 0) → v = 0) :
    Function.Injective S := by

theorem cancel_dense_range

theorem contraction_projection
    (C : H2 →L[ℂ] H3 →L[ℂ] H1)
    (P0 : H1 →L[ℂ] H1) (P1 : H2 →L[ℂ] H2) (P2 : H3 →L[ℂ] H3)

    (hleft : ∀ g h, P0 (C g h) = C g (P2 h))
    (hright : ∀ g h, P0 (C g h) = C (P1 g) h) :

claims.natural_statement: Manuscript Theorem thm:main asserts that every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of every finite order, without standardness or countable-generation assumptions. Its validity is not established by this operator-square audit.

Manuscript prop:zero-entropy-witness asserts that a least failure of higher-order mixing gives a mixing finite-alphabet zero-entropy process with lower-order mixing and a uniformly positive centered layout correlation.

Manuscript prop:saturation asserts that every array object admits an extension whose conditional-expectation energies for parameter, outside-plane, and combined data cannot increase under any further extension.

Manuscript lem:rolled-extension asserts that rolling the first array axis into local states and retaining at most k-2 parent entries gives a valid extension of the saturated object, without interchanging axes.

Manuscript prop:square-locality asserts the numbered parent-row screening kernels and all three-block grouped forms for almost every parameter square of the saturated array object. This audit assumes these assertions when proving C_OP_CORE; their derivation is unverified here.

Manuscript lem:active-exact, prop:measurable-labels, lem:finite-blocks and prop:block-witness assert that the fibre exact-line groups and parameter geometry give a nonzero finite moving-block witness over the zero-entropy process.

Manuscript prop:orbit-cancellation asserts Cesaro absolute-correlation cancellation for every coupling of a zero-entropy mixing process to an orthogonal projective-character family indexed by an automorphism orbit, using entropy cancellation, orbit alternatives, and polynomial cancellation.

Candidate assertion, not a manuscript assertion: on nine unbiased binary cells the full-support law with density 1+(sum of the three row parities plus sum of the three column parities)/8 relative to product measure satisfies all inherited square-locality hypotheses.

routes.retired_because: The softened-parity law has E[C0 C1]=0 but E[C0]E[C1]=1/64 for two distinct column parities, violating proper-column independence. It cannot refute the full square-locality implication; no manuscript flaw follows.
